chunks: Yaqub ibn Yazid from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Regarding the resident of Mecca who goes out to his family and then returns to Mecca, with what [condition] does he enter?
He said: 'If his stay in Mecca is more than six months, he does not perform Tamattu', and if it is less than six months, he may perform Tamattu'.'

key_terms.تَمَتُّع: Tamattu' (a type of Hajj combining Umrah and Hajj)
key_terms.سِتَّةِ أَشْهُرٍ: Six months (the threshold for residency status)

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for a resident of Mecca to perform Tamattu' during Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the distinction between a *Muqim* (resident) and a *Musafir* (traveler) for the purpose of performing *Hajj al-Tamattu'*, a key ritual in Shia jurisprudence. It establishes a six-month threshold: staying longer than this period reclassifies the individual as a resident who performs Hajj as a local, while a shorter stay preserves their traveler status, allowing them to combine Umrah and Hajj with the associated concessions. This ruling highlights the practical application of travel duration in determining ritual obligations during the Hajj season.
